Frequent Questions

Can graduate study be completed part-time?
Yes, in principle. Many of our students successfully complete their MS degree part-time. Currently we are not accepting part-time Ph.D. students.
top of page
Can Statistics courses be taken as a non-degree student?
Yes.
top of page
Are classes offered in the evening?
All required core courses for the MS are offered in the evening. Doctoral courses, and some courses that a student may be required to take in order to satisfy prerequisites, are offered only during the day.
top of page
May I apply using a paper form?
No.
top of page
May my referees use a paper recommendation form?
No.
top of page
I am currently pursuing a graduate degree at another university. What are the procedures for transferring to your program and can my credits be transferred?
Please see the transfer paragraph in the applications page for details on transferring.
top of page
I am an alumni/a from Rutgers MS program in Statistics. Can I take more courses?
Graduates from our program who want to take additional courses must re apply as non-degree students. F-1 students may not pursue a new degree program while on post-completion OPT. If an F-1 student wants to enroll in a new degree program, they must transfer to it and obtain a new, valid I-20 for that program. This transfer will automatically invalidate the EAD card (OPT), even though the card remains in their possession.
top of page
Can a GMAT score replace the GRE?
No, unfortunately, it cannot.
top of page
What code should be given to ETS to ensure that my TOEFL and GRE scores are correctly routed to the admissions committee?
Please specify the code for Graduate School New Brunswick programs. You are also encouraged to upload your unofficial test scores on the application portal.
top of page
What minimal TOEFL scores are required?
Minimum TOEFL scores are set by the graduate school.
top of page
I am a graduate student at Rutgers. Can I pursue the MS degree in Statistics at the same time as my current program?
Yes.
top of page
Where can the prerequisite courses be taken?
That is up to the individual. Courses may be taken at any institution of higher education.
top of page
I have not taken all the prerequisite courses. Should I still apply?
We will consider applications from students who show promise. Students lacking prerequisites may still be admitted to the program, but will need to take some of the prerequisite courses during their first semester or preceding summer. We may make satisfactory completion of prerequisite courses within the first year after admission a condition of continued status in our program.
top of page
What is the difference between a prerequisite override and a special permission number?
A prerequisite override is a note (either an email or a hard-copy form) from the graduate program to the registrar asking that a prerequisite be waived for a course. A special permission number is a code given by the program and used by a student to register, either in person or on line, to overcome many barriers to registration not including prerequisites.
top of page
Do graduate students in your program get exposure to real data analysis projects?
The Department of Statistics maintains an Office of Statistical Consulting, and interested PhD students are assigned to assist in this office, under the supervision of its director. Many MS students arrange for supervised statistical practice. The graduate director assists with linking interested students with investigators needing data analysis help, but the primary responsibility for making these connections rests with the MS student.
top of page
I am interested in pursuing a career in actuarial science. Do Rutgers Statistics degrees provide suitable preparation for actuarial exams?
That is not the purpose of our degrees. Please visit Preparation for an Actuarial Career at Rutgers for more information on courses offered which are appropriate for actuarial students.
top of page
Do Rutgers Statistics degrees provide suitable preparation for pursuing a career in financial mathematics?
Yes. We offer a degree in Financial Statistics and Risk Management. You might also consider the MS in Mathematics with the Option in Mathematical Finance program, or the MS in Quantitative Finance program, offered by the business school.
top of page
Do you have rolling admission? When can I begin the program?
Your available starting dates depend on desired program and visa status. We strongly encourage students to submit applications by the published deadlines. We cannot guarantee that applications submitted after the application deadline will be considered in time for matriculation during the term requested. Late applications may be consider, or deferred until the following term.
top of page
What is the difference between non-degree and non-matriculated admission?
Students are admitted to non-degree status when they intend to take a few courses, but do not intend to enroll in a degree program. Students are admitted to non-matriculated status when they intend to enroll in a degree program, but their appropriateness for the program is unclear.
top of page
What is the maximum number of course credits I can take in a semester?
12.
top of page
What is the minimum number of courses I can take in a semester?
Please see the minimum credit policy.
top of page
Is there a style sheet for dissertation preparation?
Yes.
top of page
My enrollment has lapsed because I did not register for one or more semesters. Can I apply to be reenrolled?
Yes.
top of page
What books will be used in my courses during the next semester?
Information on books intended for use in the upcoming semester, and on how to obtain these, may be found on the schedule page.
top of page
Can I obtain copies of statistical software from the Department or Graduate Program of Statistics?
No. Software is available via the Rutgers software portal, from a third-party vendor, or free.
top of page
I already have a terminal MS degree in Statistics from Rutgers. What do I need to do to enroll in the PhD program?
You will need to apply as a regular applicant on the graduate school website.
top of page
May undergraduates take courses offered by the Graduate Program in Statistics?
Yes, under certain conditions.
top of page
Is there provision for students at other universities to take Rutgers Statistics courses, other than as a non-matriculated student?
In some cases, yes. Please see the separate document on cross-registration.
top of page
Does your department offer programs in educational statistics, measurement, and evaluation, or in statistics education?
Activities in these areas are concentrated in the Graduate School of Education.
top of page
Will evening classes be canceled on evenings when the Rutgers football team plays a home game?
No.
top of page
Is there a procedure for readmission of students whose registration has lapsed?
Yes.
top of page
Does the Program in Statistics offer guidance on what kind of project satisfies the MS essay requirement?Yes.
top of page
Can I use my unofficial transcript for the application process?
Yes, please make sure that you upload your unofficial transcripts on the application portal.
top of page
Do I need to secure/look for a faculty member before applying and securing an assistantship?
No, but in your statement of purpose you can always mention names of faculty members whose research is of interest to you. There is also a provision in the application form where you can mention the names of any faculty member you have reached out to.
top of page
Is there a possibility of getting funding after securing admission as a TA/RA?
All students admitted to our Ph.D. program
top of page
What is the possibility of applying for a direct Ph.D. with my BSc?
We accept Ph.D. applications from students who have a four-year bachelor's degree, but the applications need to be really strong to be shortlisted or selected.
top of page
Can my TOEFLS, English language tests be waived?
If you have an undergrad or graduate degree from a US university, your TOEFL would be waived.
top of page
Do you accept submitting a recommendation though Interfolio?
We take the applications through the university's admission system, not Interfolio. Please visit https://gradstudy.rutgers.edu/apply/apply-now to apply.
top of page
About how many applicants are admitted each year?
The proportion of admitted students is small (approx. 5%) compared to the number of applications. All admitted Ph. D students are guaranteed full funding (assistantship in the form of TA/Ga, tuition remission, health insurance) for five years subject to remaining in good academic standing. The selection process is extremely competitive.
top of page
If I am not qualified for the PhD program, will I be considered for the Masters program automatically? Or do I have to submit two applications separately?
When you apply for the PhD program, there should be an option that says something like "if not selected, do you also want to be considered for the master's program"? Please choose yes for that option.
top of page
What is the maximum length of the masters program？
You need 30 credits (10 3-credit courses) to obtain the MS degree. Some students finish in three semesters (3+3+4 or 3+4+3 etc.), most students take four semesters (3+3+3+1). International students need to register for a minimum of 9 credits every semester to maintain their visa status, but they are allowed to take a reduced credit load in their final semester.
top of page
Can I waive my graduate admissions fee?
The Office of Graduate Admissions grants application fee waivers to the following groups only: active U.S. military and military veterans who plan to apply for educational benefits under the GI Bill, current Rutgers students and alumni, and participants in various scholar programs. Students are automatically reviewed for fee waiver eligibility based on the information they provide on their Rutgers graduate school application. Please visit newbrunswickgrad.rutgers.edu for more information.
